mainTopic: How a Hebrew servant is acquired with a שטר, and the ways Hebrew servants go free
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: the פסוק about a Hebrew slave sold to a נכרי means a נכרי under Jewish rule. Then the גמרא asks for the source that a Hebrew servant can be acquired בשטר. עולא learns it by comparing an אמה העבריה to a woman being married. That comparison fits רב הונא, who says the master writes the שטר, but not רב חסדא, who says the father writes it. So רב אחא בר יעקב learns it from 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים': she is acquired like slaves. The גמרא then works out why that means שטר and not חזקה, and how each אמורא reads the פסוק. Next the גמרא gives sources for the ways an עבד עברי goes free: six years, the יובל, and גרעון כסף. A ברייתא adds that he can go free with a release document, and רבא learns from this that the slave's body is owned. Finally ריש לקיש teaches that the father's death frees an אמה העבריה. The גמרא defends him against the משנה's silence by saying the משנה lists only ways of going free that have a set time. רב ספרא's explanation of סימנין continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse speaks of a gentile under Jewish authority
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the פסוק is about a נכרי who is under Jewish control. A נכרי outside Jewish control could not be forced to do anything anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is talking about a gentile who is under your authority. Maybe it means a gentile who is not under your authority? You could answer: what could be done to force him? So the verse must be talking only about a gentile who is under your authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא from the previous page. It proves that the פסוק about a Hebrew slave sold to a נכרי means a נכרי who lives under Jewish rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises another option: maybe the פסוק means a נכרי who is not under Jewish control. It rejects this with simple logic. The Torah would not command something about a person we have no power to force. So it must mean a נכרי we can actually make follow the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Under your authority, meaning under Jewish rule
But what can be done to him? (we have no power over him)

phrases.english: with a gentile who is under your authority,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּנׇכְרִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ תַּחַת יָדֶךָ?
phrases.english: or is it only with a gentile who is not under your authority?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ, וְכִי מָה אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ?
phrases.english: You can say: but what could be done to him?
So the verse is speaking only of
a gentile who is under your authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵין הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּנׇכְרִי שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ תַּחַת יָדֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק about a Hebrew slave sold to a נכרי refers to a נכרי under Jewish authority.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a servant is acquired through a document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'ובשטר' and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and through a document.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule that a Hebrew servant can be acquired with a document and asks where this comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed ways to acquire a Hebrew servant: with money or with a שטר. Money already has a source, so now the גמרא wants a source for the שטר. This question sets up the answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: "And through a document." From where do we derive this?
phrases.notes: The first word is quoted from the משנה, which says a Hebrew servant can be acquired with money or with a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a Hebrew servant can be acquired through a שטר.

steps.title: עולא compares the maidservant to a woman being married
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns it from 'אם אחרת יקח לו'. The פסוק places אמה העבריה next to 'another' woman being married, and that woman can be acquired with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The verse says, 'If he takes another for himself.' The verse compares her to another woman. Just as another woman is acquired with a document, a Hebrew maidservant is also acquired with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers with a היקש. Because the פסוק calls a new wife 'another,' the maidservant is grouped together with a wife. So whatever works for a wife also works for the maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אחרת' (another) suggests that the first woman, the maidservant, is in the same category as the second, a woman being married. A woman can be married with a שטר. So the maidservant can be acquired with a שטר too.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a sage of the גמרא
He compared her (a היקש: linking two cases so they share the same laws)
Another (woman), here meaning a woman being married

phrases.english: Ulla said: The verse says:
"If he takes another for himself"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:10

phrases.english: the verse compared her to another woman,
just as another woman is acquired through a document,
so too a Hebrew maidservant is acquired through a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש from 'אם אחרת יקח לו': the maidservant is like a wife, who is acquired with a שטר.

steps.title: The comparison only works if the master writes the document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: עולא's comparison fits the view that the master writes the maidservant's שטר. But it does not fit the view that the father writes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the master writes the Hebrew maidservant's document. But for the one who says the father writes it, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's source. The comparison to marriage seems to work only according to one opinion about who writes the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In marriage, the husband, who is the one acquiring, writes the שטר. If the master, the one acquiring, writes the maidservant's שטר, the two cases match. If the father, the one selling, writes it, then it is more like a sale document, and the comparison to marriage falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
What is there to say? (this view seems to have a problem)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
the master writes the document of a Hebrew maidservant,
but according to the one who says: the father writes it,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's היקש in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's היקש comparing אמה העבריה to a woman being married.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father writes the שטר, it is not like a marriage שטר, which the husband writes. So the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: The dispute: who writes the maidservant's document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for the two opinions: רב הונא says the master writes it, and רב חסדא says the father writes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: Who writes the document of a Hebrew maidservant? רב הונא says: the master writes it. רב חסדא says: the father writes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting the actual dispute between אמוראים. This shows the 'father writes it' view really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step is background for the challenge. It names who holds each view: רב הונא says the master, and רב חסדא says the father. Now the question against עולא can be aimed directly at רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (a dispute between אמוראים)
An אמורא who says the master writes it
An אמורא who says the father writes it

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיתְּמַר: שְׁטַר אָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה, מִי כּוֹתְבוֹ?
phrases.english: As it was stated: The document of a Hebrew maidservant, who writes it?
Rav Huna says: The master writes it.
Rav Ḥisda says: The father writes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: שְׁטַר אָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה, מִי כּוֹתְבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the two views mentioned in the challenge of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the master writes the שטר. רב חסדא: the father writes the שטר.

steps.title: The challenge restated against רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its question with names: עולא's source fits רב הונא, but what is the source according to רב חסדא?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב הונא. But for רב חסדא, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the challenge, now naming רב הונא and רב חסדא. This sets up the need for a new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The general challenge from step 4 is simply attached to the named sages from step 5. The problem is that, according to רב חסדא, we still have no source for acquiring with a שטר. The next step gives one.

phrases.english: This works well according to Rav Huna,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Rav Ḥisda, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the challenge of step 4 using the names from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for acquiring with a שטר according to רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא's marriage comparison needs the acquirer to write the שטר, and רב חסדא says the father writes it.

steps.title: A new source: she is acquired like slaves
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns it from 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים'. She does not go out like slaves, but she is acquired like them, and slaves are acquired with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says, 'She shall not go out as the slaves go out.' This means she does not go out like them, but she is acquired like slaves. And what is that? A document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different source that works even for רב חסדא. It does not depend on comparing the maidservant to marriage at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she does not go free the way slaves do. The גמרא reads this as teaching that leaving is different, but being acquired is the same. Slaves can be acquired with a שטר, so she can be too, no matter who writes it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the new source
She shall not go out as the slaves go out

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for acquiring a Hebrew servant with a שטר. עולא compares her to marriage, which works for רב הונא. רב אחא בר יעקב says she is acquired like slaves, which works even for רב חסדא.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says she does NOT go out like slaves. The lesson is the opposite side: only her leaving is different, but her acquisition is the same as slaves.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said: The verse says:
"She shall not go out as the slaves go out"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7. Here 'slaves' means non-Jewish (כנעני) slaves.

phrases.english: but she is acquired the way slaves are acquired.
And what is that? A document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by giving a new source that works for רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source from a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only source for acquiring with a שטר was the marriage comparison, which fails for רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' teaches that she is acquired like slaves, with a שטר, according to every view.

steps.title: Why not say she is acquired with possession like slaves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב: if she is acquired like slaves, maybe the method is חזקה and not שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe we should say: she is acquired the way slaves are acquired, and what is that? חזקה (possession)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אחא בר יעקב's answer. If an אמה העבריה is acquired 'like slaves', why assume that means שטר? Slaves are also acquired with חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 learned: she does not go out like slaves, but she is acquired like them. The problem is that slaves have more than one way of being acquired. So the פסוק alone does not tell us which slave method applies to her.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (a way to suggest a different reading)
The ways a כנעני slave is acquired
Acquiring by acting as the owner, for example having the slave do work for you

phrases.english: But say: but she is acquired
like the acquisition of slaves,
and what is that? Possession!
phrases.notes: A slave can be acquired when he does a job for his new master, like helping him get dressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אֲבָל נִקְנֵית הִיא כְּקִנְיַן עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רב אחא בר יעקב's derivation in step 7 should be read
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's reading of 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' as teaching שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaves are acquired in more than one way, so 'acquired like slaves' could just as well mean חזקה.

steps.title: Only Canaanite slaves are acquired with possession
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק about כנעני slaves limits חזקה to them alone, so it cannot apply to an אמה העבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall pass them down as an inheritance to your children after you.' 'Them' can be acquired with חזקה, but no other slave can be acquired with חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזקה cannot be the method. A פסוק says that only 'them', the כנעני slaves, are acquired that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותם' (them) is read as a limit. חזקה belongs only to כנעני slaves, who are treated like inherited land. So an אמה העבריה cannot be acquired with חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (bringing a source from the תורה)
And you shall pass down as an inheritance
Another (here: any slave other than a כנעני slave)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And you shall bequeath them to your children after you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46

phrases.english: them through possession,
but not another through possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Acquired like slaves' might mean acquired with חזקה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותם' limits חזקה to כנעני slaves, so it cannot apply to her

steps.title: Then limit the document to Canaanite slaves too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same limit back: maybe 'אותם' also means only כנעני slaves are acquired with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: 'them' are acquired with a שטר, and no other slave is acquired with a שטר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer of step 9 against itself. If 'אותם' limits חזקה, it could just as easily limit שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the word 'אותם' points only to חזקה. If it can cut out חזקה, it could also cut out שטר. Then we would lose the source that she is acquired with a שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document used to make a קנין

phrases.english: But say: them through a document,
but not another through a document!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אוֹתָם בִּשְׁטָר, וְלֹא אַחֵר בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limiting reading used in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'אותם' to limit only חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word could limit שטר, which would take away the source for her being acquired with a שטר.

steps.title: The פסוק 'she shall not go out like slaves' must teach something
steps.stepSummary: 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' shows she is acquired like slaves in at least one way, so both methods cannot be excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'She shall not go out the way slaves go out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing back to the פסוק of רב אחא בר יעקב. That פסוק shows she shares at least one way of being acquired with slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אותם' cut out both חזקה and שטר, 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' would teach nothing about how she is acquired. So 'אותם' can only cut out one of the two methods.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (pointing to a פסוק that answers the question)
The way slaves go out (go free)

phrases.english: Isn't it written: "She shall not go out as the men slaves do"?
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7. This is the same פסוק רב אחא בר יעקב used in step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing that one method must stay
steps.terutzResolutionType: The second פסוק must have a purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותם' could cut out both שטר and חזקה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' requires her to share one slave method, so only one is excluded

steps.title: Why choose the document over possession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we decided the shared method is שטר and the excluded one is חזקה, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to choose it this way?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next few steps. We now know one method is included and one is left out, but which is which?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים leave a choice. Either she is acquired with a שטר and not with חזקה, or with חזקה and not with a שטר. The גמרא wants a reason for picking שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why did you choose one side over the other?)

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why include שטר and leave out חזקה, and not the opposite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 11: once one method is included, which one is it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A reason to include שטר rather than חזקה
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' includes שטר and 'אותם' excludes חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two פסוקים could just as well be read the other way: she is acquired with חזקה like slaves, and 'אותם' limits שטר to כנעני slaves.

steps.title: A document is stronger because it can end a marriage
steps.stepSummary: Logic says to include שטר, because a שטר is strong enough to release a Jewish woman from marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense: a שטר should be the one included, because a שטר can release a Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason from logic. A שטר is a strong tool, since a גט, which is a שטר, ends a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק includes one thing and leaves out another, we include the stronger one. A שטר has the special power to release a בת ישראל, so it is the better choice to include.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (an answer from logic)

phrases.english: It stands to reason,
a document should be included,
since it releases a Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.terutzMaskana: שטר is stronger since it can release a בת ישראל, so it is the one included

steps.title: Possession has its own special power
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the other way: חזקה is also strong, since it alone acquires a convert's ownerless property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! חזקה should be included, because it acquires the property of a גר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the logic of step 13. חזקה also has a special power, so maybe it should be the one included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גר dies with no Jewish heirs, his property belongs to no one. It can be taken with חזקה, and a שטר does not work there. So חזקה has its own strength, and step 13's logic does not settle the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of a convert (here: one who died with no Jewish heirs)

phrases.english: On the contrary,
possession should be included,
since it acquires the property of a convert!
phrases.notes: When a גר dies with no heirs, his things belong to no one, and the first person to take hold of them gets them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical reason given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שטר is the stronger method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזקה also has a unique power (acquiring נכסי הגר), so it could be the one to include.

steps.title: Possession is never used for marriage
steps.stepSummary: In marriage at least, חזקה never works, but a שטר does, so שטר fits better for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: In marriage, at least, we do not find חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counter-argument. Whatever power חזקה has, it is never used to make a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה העבריה is closely tied to marriage, since she may end up married to her master or his son. A שטר works for marriage and חזקה does not, so שטר is the better match for her.

phrases.english: With regard to marriage, at least,
we do not find it.
phrases.notes: He means we never find חזקה making a marriage, while a שטר can.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counter-argument of step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקה is as strong as שטר and could be the one included
steps.terutzMaskana: For marriage-related acquisitions only שטר works, so we include שטר

steps.title: Second answer: 'אם אחרת' points to the document
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the פסוק 'אם אחרת' tells us to compare her to a married woman, who is acquired with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: this is what 'אם אחרת' is useful for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to 'why choose שטר?'. The פסוק 'אם אחרת', which עולא used, tells us which slave method to pick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, for רב חסדא, 'אם אחרת' does not teach שטר alone. It works together with 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' and settles the choice. Since she is linked to a woman acquired for marriage, we pick the method used in marriage, a שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (a second answer)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, she is acquired with a שטר because 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' compares her to slaves. חזקה is left out because 'אותם' limits it to כנעני slaves. We pick שטר over חזקה either because only שטר works for marriage, or because 'אם אחרת' points to it.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
for this purpose "if another" is effective.
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק עולא used back in step 3, comparing her to another woman being married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְהָכִי אַהֲנִי אִם אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic alone cannot decide between שטר and חזקה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אם אחרת' compares her to marriage, so שטר is the method included

steps.title: What does רב הונא learn from 'she shall not go out like slaves'?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב הונא learns שטר from 'אם אחרת', the גמרא asks what he does with 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא, what does he learn from this פסוק, 'She shall not go out the way slaves go out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion. רב הונא already has a source for שטר, so the פסוק of רב אחא בר יעקב must teach him something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the תורה must teach something. If רב הונא does not need 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' for שטר, the גמרא wants to know what he uses it for.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And רב הונא,
this verse, "She shall not go out as the men slaves do",
what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא, הַאי לֹא תֵצֵא כְּצֵאת הָעֲבָדִים מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רב חסדא's source, asks how רב הונא uses the same פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב הונא learns from 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים'

steps.title: She does not go free through loss of a limb
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא uses the פסוק to teach that she does not go free through ראשי אברים, the way a כנעני slave does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק to teach that she does not go free through injury to her limbs, the way a slave does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא uses the פסוק for a different law. A כנעני slave goes free if his master knocks out a tooth or an eye, but she does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, 'she shall not go out like slaves' is read literally, as being about going free. It teaches that one way a slave goes free does not apply to her. It does not teach anything about how she is acquired.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
Main limbs and body parts (like a tooth, eye, finger)

phrases.english: He needs that verse:
that she does not go out
through injury to her limbs like a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּרָאשֵׁי אֵבָרִים כְּעֶבֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא learns that an אמה העבריה does not go free through ראשי אברים

steps.title: Where does רב חסדא learn the limb law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רב חסדא used this פסוק for שטר, so where does he learn the ראשי אברים law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: A very short question that sets up the final answer. רב חסדא already used the פסוק for שטר, so does he lose the law about limbs?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראשי אברים law is accepted by everyone. If רב חסדא used the פסוק for שטר, the גמרא wants to know where he gets this law from.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
A Jewish girl sold as a maidservant by her father
And רב חסדא? (a short way to ask what he holds)

phrases.english: And רב חסדא?
phrases.notes: He means: where does רב חסדא learn that she does not go free through her limbs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of step 17 around onto רב חסדא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב חסדא's source for the ראשי אברים law

steps.title: The extra wording teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said 'כעבדים'. The extra word 'כצאת' shows it teaches two things: the limb law and the שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it only taught one thing, the פסוק should have said 'She shall not go out like slaves'. Why does it say 'the way slaves go out'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק has extra wording. So רב חסדא learns both laws from it: no going free through limbs, and acquisition with a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shorter wording, 'כעבדים', would have been enough for one lesson. The longer 'כצאת העבדים' is extra, and that extra word is used for a second lesson. This way רב חסדא loses nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק write (it should have said)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא learns שטר from 'אם אחרת' and uses 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים' for ראשי אברים. רב חסדא learns both from 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים', because the wording 'כצאת' is extra.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
"She shall not go out like the slaves",
why "as the slaves go out"?
Learn two things from it.
phrases.notes: The two lessons: she doesn't go free through her limbs, and she is acquired with a שטר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא: לֹא תֵּצֵא כָּעֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra wording 'כצאת' lets רב חסדא learn both the ראשי אברים law and the שטר law from one פסוק

steps.title: Going free after six years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an עבד עברי goes free after six years and gives the פסוק it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he acquires himself (goes free) through years. This is because it is written: 'Six years he shall work, and in the seventh he shall go out free.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the ways an עבד עברי goes free. It starts with the first way, six years of work, and shows its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'קונה את עצמו' means the slave 'acquires himself', so he becomes his own owner again. The פסוק says plainly that after six years of work he goes out in the seventh. So the rule of 'שנים' comes straight from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires himself, meaning he goes free
Years, here the six years of work

phrases.english: And he acquires himself through years.
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה. 'Acquires himself' just means he goes free.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Six years he shall work,
and in the seventh, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות כא:ב. The rest of the פסוק says he goes out free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שטר and ראשי אברים discussion of the אמה and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי goes free after six years, based on 'שש שנים יעבד ובשבעת'.

steps.title: Going free at the יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the source for the rule that an עבד עברי goes free in the יובל year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he goes free in the יובל. This is because it is written: 'Until the יובל year he shall work with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא covers the second way out, the יובל, and gives its פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק sets the יובל as the end point of his work. So even if six years have not passed yet, he goes free when the יובל arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: The fiftieth year, when slaves go free

phrases.english: In the Jubilee. As it is written:
'Until the Jubilee year he shall work with you.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:מ

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the משנה, with the same pattern of quote plus פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי goes free at the יובל, based on 'עד שנת היובל יעבד עמך'.

steps.title: Going free by paying for the remaining years
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from 'והפדה' that a slave can go free early by paying the value of the years still left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he goes free by deducting money. חזקיה said: the פסוק says 'and he shall let her be redeemed.' This teaches that she subtracts from her redemption price and goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives חזקיה's source for the third way out, גרעון כסף, which means paying only for the years that are left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original price covered all six years. If some years have already been worked, their value is taken off, and the slave pays only the rest to go free. חזקיה finds this in the word 'והפדה', which means redemption is possible partway through.

keyTerms.meaning: Deducting money, paying only for the remaining time
'And he shall let her be redeemed'
The אמורא who teaches this source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get thrown that the פסוק says 'her'. It is about the אמה העבריה, and the same rule is used for the male slave in the משנה.

phrases.english: Through deduction of money.
חזקיה said: because the verse says: 'And he shall let her be redeemed' –
phrases.notes: שמות כא:ח

phrases.english: this teaches that she deducts from her redemption price and goes out.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, so read it as 'she deducts'.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּגִרְעוֹן כֶּסֶף. אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third clause of the משנה. This time the source is given in the name of an אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave may go free early by paying the value of the remaining years ('והפדה').

steps.title: A ברייתא adds money, money's worth, and a document
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the slave can free himself with כסף, שוה כסף, or a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And he acquires himself with money, with something worth money, and with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists three ways the slave can buy his own freedom. This sets up the next question about where each one comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke about deducting money. The ברייתא adds two more ways besides plain money: an object worth money, and a שטר. The שטר is the new and surprising item, and it is what the גמרא will ask about.

phrases.english: It was taught: And he acquires himself
with money, with something worth money, and with a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that widens the list of ways the slave can redeem himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי can redeem himself with כסף, שוה כסף, or שטר.

steps.title: Money and money's worth are clear, but what is the document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the sources for כסף and שוה כסף, then asks what kind of שטר the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money is understandable, as it is written: 'From the money he was bought for.' Something worth money is also understandable, because the תורה says 'he shall return his redemption', to include things worth money like money. But this document, what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the first two items in the ברייתא and gives their sources. Then it asks what case the שטר could be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מכסף מקנתו' covers money. The wording 'ישיב גאלתו' is read as including anything of value, so it covers שוה כסף. The שטר has no clear source, and it is not clear what such a document would even do. That is the question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the money he was bought for'
What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: It is understandable regarding money,
as it is written: 'From the money he was bought for';
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:נא

phrases.english: something worth money too,
'He shall return his redemption,' the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא כה:נא.

phrases.english: to include something worth money as being like money;
but this document, what is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines each item of the ברייתא from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of שטר could free an עבד עברי, separate from money?

steps.title: A note of debt for his value is just money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the slave wrote his master a note owing his value, then rejects this because that is the same as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that he wrote him a document for his value, that is the same as money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation of the שטר and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שטר is just a note promising to pay the slave's value, then what frees him is really the money owed. That would not be a separate way from כסף, so the ברייתא would have no reason to list it on its own. The next step gives a different explanation of the שטר.

phrases.english: If you say that he wrote him
a document for his value,
phrases.notes: He means a note saying the slave owes the master his price.

phrases.english: that is the same as money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question in step 25 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects explaining the שטר as a note of debt for the slave's value.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A note of debt is really a payment of money, so it would not be a separate item from כסף in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The document is a release document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the שטר in the ברייתא is a document of release written by the master.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means a document of release.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the idea of a debt note, the גמרא says the שטר is a release document that the master writes to free the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 showed that a note owing money is really just money, so it cannot be a separate way to go free. A release document is different: it is not payment, it is the master formally letting the slave go.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; a new answer replaces the one just rejected

phrases.english: Rather, [it is a document of] release.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 26 rejected the debt-note idea.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of שטר frees an עבד עברי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A release document written by the master.

steps.title: Why is a document needed to free him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the master needs a document at all, when he could just tell the slave 'go' in front of two witnesses or a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a document? Let him say to him in front of two people: 'Go.' Or let him say in front of a בית דין: 'Go.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer: freeing someone should be possible with simple words in front of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slave only owes the master work, like a debt, the master could just give it up out loud. Witnesses or a בית דין would be enough proof. So why would a written document be needed?

keyTerms.meaning: In front of two people (two witnesses)

phrases.english: Why do I need a document?
Let him say to him in front of two [witnesses]: 'Go!'
Or else, in front of a court: 'Go!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a release document is needed to free an עבד עברי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spoken words in front of witnesses should be enough to release the slave, so a document seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The master owns the slave's body
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from this that the master owns the body of an עבד עברי, so a master who gives up the remaining money owed does not free the slave just by saying so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This shows that an עבד עברי's body is owned. And if a master gives up his deduction, the deduction is not given up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by learning a rule from the ברייתא: the slave is truly owned, not just in debt, so freeing him needs a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain debt can be cancelled with words. But the master owns the slave's body itself, so saying 'I give up what you owe me' does not undo that ownership. Only a formal document can free him.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows; we learn from here
His deduction; the money for the years left to work

steps.whatToRemember: The body of an עבד עברי is owned by his master, so he cannot be freed by words alone. He needs a release document.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that an עבד עברי's body is owned, explains why his release works like a legal transfer and not like cancelling a debt.

phrases.english: רבא said: This shows
that a Hebrew slave's body is owned,
and a master who gave up his deduction —
phrases.notes: The deduction is what the slave would pay to leave early, as in step 23.

phrases.english: his deduction is not given up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by learning a rule from it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learns a new legal rule that explains why the document is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Words in front of witnesses should be enough to free the slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave's body is owned, so only a document of release frees him.

steps.title: The father's death frees the maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the extra way an אמה העבריה goes free, and ריש לקיש adds that her father's death also frees her from her master, through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says an אמה העבריה has more than him. ריש לקיש said: An אמה העבריה frees herself from her master when her father dies. This is a קל וחומר: if signs of maturity, which do not take her out of her father's control, do take her out of the master's control, then death, which does take her out of her father's control, surely takes her out of the master's control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, and ריש לקיש adds another way an אמה העבריה goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signs of maturity are a weaker release: she still stays partly under her father's control, yet they free her from the master. Her father's death fully ends his control, so it should surely free her from the master too.

keyTerms.meaning: She has more than him (an extra way to go free)
Logic from a weaker case to a stronger one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'father' and 'master'. The father sold her; the master bought her. The question is whether her father's death frees her from the master.

phrases.english: She has more than him: a Hebrew maidservant.
ריש לקיש said:
A Hebrew maidservant acquires herself
through the death of the father, from the master's control,
through a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה סִימָנִין שֶׁאֵין מוֹצִיאִין מֵרְשׁוּת אָב –
phrases.english: If signs, which do not take her out of the father's control —
do take her out of the master's control,
death, which takes her out of the father's control —
is it not logical that it takes her out of the master's control?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה קוֹנָה אֶת עַצְמָהּ בְּמִיתַת הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the line in the משנה about the אמה העבריה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אמה העבריה goes free from her master when her father dies, learned through a קל וחומר from signs of maturity.

steps.title: The משנה does not mention the father's death
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא challenges ריש לקיש: the משנה lists only signs of maturity as her extra way out. If the father's death also frees her, it should be listed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא objected: 'She has more than him: an אמה העבריה acquires herself through signs.' If ריש לקיש is right, let it also teach the father's death!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא attacks ריש לקיש's rule from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists what the maidservant has that the male slave lacks, and gives only signs of maturity. If her father's death were another such way, the משנה should have listed it, so its silence seems to argue against ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: רב הושעיא objected:
A Hebrew maidservant has more than him,
in that she acquires herself through signs.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if ריש לקיש is right that the father's death frees her.

phrases.english: let it also teach the death of the father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's rule from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that the father's death frees the אמה העבריה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists her extra ways out and leaves out the father's death, which suggests it does not free her.

steps.title: The משנה left some things out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה taught some cases and left others out, so its silence proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by saying the משנה's list is not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A list in a משנה does not have to include everything. The father's death could be one of the cases the משנה chose not to mention.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught and left some out

phrases.english: It taught and left [some] out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הושעיא's challenge in step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's list includes every way she goes free.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left some cases out, so the father's death may be one of them.

steps.title: What else did the משנה leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what other case the משנה left out, since 'it left some out' needs at least one more missing case besides this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did it leave out, that it would leave this out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer of step 32 by asking for another missing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim 'it taught and left some out' is only believable if we can point to another case that is also missing. If the father's death is the only missing case, the answer looks weak.

phrases.english: What [else] did it leave out, that it left out this?
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes a תנא would not leave out just one case. It wants a second one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer of step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Another case the משנה left out, to support 'it taught and left some out'.

steps.title: It left out the master's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the other missing case is the master's death, which also frees the אמה העבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It left out the master's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second missing case: the death of the master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master's death also frees the maidservant, yet it is not listed in this line of the משנה. If that is a second missing case, then the father's death could be missing too.

phrases.english: It left out the death of the master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The master's death is another case the משנה left out.

steps.title: The master's death does not count as left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: the master's death also frees a man, so it does not belong in a list of things only she has.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the master's death, that is not something left out. Since it also applies to a man, it does not teach it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 34: the master's death was never supposed to be in this list at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line of the משנה only lists what the maidservant has more than a man. The master's death also frees a man (the משנה teaches it for the נרצע), so it is not an extra for her. That means it is not really 'left out', so the 'it left some out' answer is weakened. Steps 36-37 take up the question again.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it also applies to a man

phrases.english: If it is because of the death of the master,
that is not something left out,
since it also applies to a man —
phrases.notes: The משנה teaches that a נרצע, a slave whose ear was pierced, goes free when his master dies.

phrases.english: it does not teach it [here].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם מִיתַת הָאָדוֹן, לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the master's death as the second missing case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The list only covers things the maidservant has and a man does not. The master's death also frees a man, so it never belonged in the list.

steps.title: Then the משנה should list the father's death
steps.stepSummary: Since the master's death does not count as a second missing case, the original challenge comes back: the משנה should list the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, let the משנה teach it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב הושעיא's challenge. If 'the משנה left some cases out' does not work, the משנה should have listed the father's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 claimed the משנה simply left cases out. Step 35 showed there is no second missing case of this kind, so that answer falls away. The question comes back: if the father's death frees her, why isn't it listed? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so / rather (the earlier answer failed)
Let it teach (let the משנה list it)

phrases.english: But if so, let it teach it!
phrases.notes: 'It' here means the father's death as a way she goes free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because the rejection in Step 35 cancels the answer from Step 32, the challenge from Step 31 returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the father's death frees the אמה העבריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father's death frees her and the משנה did not leave other cases out, the משנה's silence is a problem.

steps.title: The משנה lists only things with a set time
steps.stepSummary: The תנא lists only ways of going free that have a set time. The father's death has no set time, so he left it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא teaches a matter that has a set time. He does not teach a matter that has no set time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason the father's death is missing. The משנה only lists things that happen at a set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different kind of answer from Step 32. The silence is not random; the list has a rule. Years of service and the יובל come at known times, but nobody knows when a father will die, so it does not fit the list.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קִצְבָה קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: The tanna teaches a matter that has a set time,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָה – לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: a matter that has no set time, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קִצְבָה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed challenge from Step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the rule behind the משנה's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should list every way she goes free, including the father's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only ways of going free that have a set time. The father's death has none, so it is left out.

steps.title: But signs of maturity have no set time either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: סימנין come at different ages for different girls, so they have no set time, yet the משנה lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But signs of maturity have no set time, and the משנה lists them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'set time' rule. It points to a case already in the משנה that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Girls develop סימנין at different ages, so there seems to be no fixed time. If the משנה still lists סימנין, the 'set time' rule cannot explain why it skips the father's death.

phrases.english: But there are signs of maturity,
which have no set time, and it teaches them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא סִימָנִין דְּאֵין לָהֶם קִצְבָה וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule given in Step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the משנה lists only things with a set time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סימנין have no set time but appear in the list. So the rule does not hold.

steps.title: Signs have no upper limit, but they do have a set time
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that סימנין have no upper limit, but they still have a set time in another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא says: They have no set time at the top end, but they do have a set time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא defends the 'set time' rule. He explains that סימנין do have a set time, just not a maximum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a girl reaches the right age, the סימנין can show up at any later point. That is why there is no upper limit. But רב ספרא says there is still a set time in another direction, so סימנין can stay in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge
At the top end (an upper limit)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ספרא is not saying סימנין have no set time at all. He agrees they have no upper limit, but he holds they do have a set time.

phrases.english: Rav Safra says:
they have no set time at the top end,
phrases.notes: Once she is old enough, the signs can come at any later time.

phrases.english: but they do have a set time

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא אֵין לָהֶם קִצְבָה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 38 and saves the rule from Step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction (no upper limit, but still a set time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סימנין have no set time at all, so they break the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: סימנין lack only an upper limit. They still have a set time, so the rule stands.
